exercises.summary: Integer types, their ranges, and what signed overflow does (UBSan catches it).

tests.name: 25 lakh home loan at 9.25% for 20 years

hints: Run the starter on the first test. UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer stops it with `signed integer overflow`. An `int` holds at most 2,147,483,647.
`100000 * 100 * 850` is already 8.5 billion. Use `long long` (at least 64 bits) for every variable in the calculation, and `%lld` in scanf and printf.

exercises.title: A growable array with realloc
exercises.summary: malloc/realloc/free, doubling growth, and leak-free ownership (ASan + LeakSanitizer).
hints: When `v->len == v->cap`, compute `new_cap = v->cap == 0 ? 4 : v->cap * 2`.
Never write `v->data = realloc(v->data, ...)`. If realloc fails it returns NULL and you lose the old block (a leak). Store the result in a temporary first.
`vec_free` must call `free(v->data)` and reset all three fields. LeakSanitizer fails the test if any block is still allocated at exit.

exercises.title: Fix the buffer overflow
exercises.summary: Undefined behaviour from strcpy, and a bounded copy that always terminates.

tests.name: fits, too long, empty, exactly cap

hints: Run the starter on the first test. AddressSanitizer reports `stack-buffer-overflow`, the line that wrote out of bounds, and which variable (`id`) was overrun.
Compute `n = strlen(src)`. If `n > cap - 1`, copy only `cap - 1` bytes. Then write the terminating `'\0'` yourself at `dst[n]`.
Handle `cap == 0` first: then there is no room even for the terminator, so return -1 without writing.

exercises.title: A chained hash map
exercises.summary: Linked lists, hashing, ownership of keys, and freeing everything (mini project 1.15).
hints: The bucket for a key is `hash(key) % NBUCKETS`. Each bucket is a singly linked list of `Entry`.
A helper that returns `Entry **` (the address of the link pointing at the entry) makes delete easy: `*link = e->next;` unlinks e wherever it is.
The map owns its keys: copy each key with `malloc(strlen(key) + 1)` and `memcpy`, and free both the key and the entry on delete and in map_free. (`strdup` is POSIX, not C17.)

exercises.title: RAII: a lease that always gets released
exercises.summary: Constructors acquire, destructors release, even when an exception is thrown. No copies.

tests.name: release on success, on exception, and in reverse order

hints: The first build fails on purpose: the two static_asserts say Lease must not be copyable. `Lease(const Lease&) = delete;` and `Lease& operator=(const Lease&) = delete;` fix that.
Look at the expected output for LN-2: `release LN-2` prints BEFORE `error: ...`. While the exception travels up to the catch, C++ destroys every local object it leaves behind (stack unwinding).
Objects in one scope are destroyed in reverse order of construction. That is why batch-B is released before batch-A.

exercises.title: A move-only buffer (rule of five)
exercises.summary: Delete copies, write noexcept move constructor and move assignment, keep ownership exact.

tests.name: moves transfer ownership, nothing leaks or double-frees

hints: Move constructor: copy the pointer and size from `other`, then set `other.data_ = nullptr; other.size_ = 0;`. Do not touch `live`: no block was created or destroyed.
Move assignment: if `this != &other`, release your own block (`if (data_) --live; delete[] data_;`), then steal other's exactly like the move constructor.
Mark both `noexcept`. std::vector only moves elements when it grows if the move constructor cannot throw; otherwise it copies (and here copying is deleted).

exercises.title: Break a shared_ptr cycle
exercises.summary: Reference counts, the control block, and why back-pointers must be weak_ptr.

tests.name: everything is destroyed, at the right time

hints: Run the starter. The use_count is 3 and nothing is ever destroyed: Customer holds the Loans, and each Loan holds the Customer. LeakSanitizer reports the leak at exit.
Make `owner` a `std::weak_ptr<Customer>`. A weak_ptr watches the control block without keeping the object alive.
To use it: `if (auto c = owner.lock()) return c->name;`. lock() gives a shared_ptr if the object still exists and an empty one if it is gone.

exercises.title: A fixed-capacity ring buffer template
exercises.summary: Class templates with a type and a size parameter; modular index arithmetic.

tests.name: ints overwrite the oldest, strings too

hints: Keep two numbers: `head_` (where the oldest item is) and `count_` (how many are stored). The next free slot is `(head_ + count_) % N`.
When full, overwrite `items_[head_]` and move head forward: `head_ = (head_ + 1) % N`. count_ stays N.
`operator[](i)` returns `items_[(head_ + i) % N]`.

exercises.title: Top-K words with unordered_map and sort
exercises.summary: Hash maps, copying into a vector, and sorting with a two-key comparator.

tests.name: ties broken alphabetically
stdin: The loan was approved. The LOAN amount: 500000.

tests.name: k larger than the number of words

hints: Build each word character by character: if `std::isalpha((unsigned char)c)`, append `std::tolower` of it; otherwise, if the current word is not empty, count it and clear it. Do not forget the last word on the line.
Copy the map into `std::vector<std::pair<std::string, int>>` and sort with a lambda: `a.second != b.second ? a.second > b.second : a.first < b.first`.
unordered_map has no order at all. Iterating it directly would give a different order on another standard library.

exercises.summary: virtual, override, virtual destructors and dispatch through a base pointer.

tests.name: each product uses its own rate

hints: Run the starter: every loan says `generic` and 1200 bps. Without `virtual`, a call through a `Loan*` is bound at compile time to Loan's version.
Add `virtual` in the base class and `override` in each derived class. `override` makes the compiler check that you really override something.
`yearly_interest()` is not virtual, yet it starts returning the right number. It calls `rate_bps()`, and that call now goes through the vtable.

exercises.title: Fix the data race
exercises.summary: Shared counters across threads; ThreadSanitizer finds the race, atomics or a mutex fix it.

tests.name: exact totals and no race reported

hints: Run the starter. ThreadSanitizer prints `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race` with the two conflicting accesses and the threads that made them, then exits with code 66.
`++approved` is three steps: load, add, store. Two threads can both load 41, both store 42, and one increment is lost.
Either make both counters `std::atomic<long long>`, or protect both updates with one `std::mutex`. A mutex is the better choice when two values must change together.

exercises.title: A blocking bounded queue
exercises.summary: mutex + two condition variables, wait with a predicate, and clean shutdown with close().
hints: push: `std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lk(m_); not_full_.wait(lk, [&]{ return closed_ || q_.size() < cap_; });`. The predicate form handles spurious wake-ups for you.
pop: wait on `not_empty_` until `closed_ || !q_.empty()`. If the queue is still empty after waking, it was closed and drained: return std::nullopt.
After push adds an item, `not_empty_.notify_one()`. After pop removes one, `not_full_.notify_one()`. close() must `notify_all()` on both, or sleeping threads never wake.
exercises.phaseTitle: Phase 4: Concurrency deep dive

exercises.title: A reader-writer store with shared_mutex
exercises.summary: Many readers at once, one writer at a time: the tcpkv store's locking.
hints: Readers: `std::shared_lock<std::shared_mutex> lk(m_);`. Many threads can hold a shared lock at the same time.
Writers: `std::unique_lock<std::shared_mutex> lk(m_);`. This waits until no reader or writer holds the lock.
`m_` is declared `mutable` so that const member functions like get() and size() can still lock it.

exercises.title: Fix the login query with a covering index
exercises.summary: Read EXPLAIN, design a composite index with the right leading column, cover the query with INCLUDE.

tests.name: login lookup is an Index Only Scan
tests.query: EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF) SELECT user_id, status FROM app_users WHERE branch_code = 'BR007' AND user_code = 'U00042';

tests.name: branch_code leads the index (branch-only lookups can use it too)
tests.query: SELECT bool_or(split_part(split_part(indexdef, '(', 2), ',', 1) = 'branch_code') AS branch_code_leads FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'app_users' AND indexname <> 'app_users_pkey';

tests.name: the query still returns the right user
tests.query: SELECT user_id, status FROM app_users WHERE branch_code = 'BR007' AND user_code = 'U00042';

hints: Run the starter: the plan says `Seq Scan on app_users` and `Rows Removed by Filter: 39999`. It reads every row to find one.
A composite B-tree index on `(branch_code, user_code)` turns that into an index lookup. Put `branch_code` first: an index can only be searched efficiently from its leading column.
To make it an Index Only Scan, the index must also hold the columns the query returns: `INCLUDE (user_id, status)`. Then PostgreSQL never visits the table at all.

exercises.title: Loan validation in PL/pgSQL
exercises.summary: A stored function with SELECT INTO, FOUND, IF/RETURN and an aggregate check.

tests.name: written in PL/pgSQL
tests.query: SELECT l.lanname FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_language l ON l.oid = p.prolang WHERE p.proname = 'validate_loan';

hints: `SELECT * INTO v_customer FROM customers WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id;` then `IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN 'NO_CUSTOMER'; END IF;`.
The rules are checked in order and the first one that fails wins. A blocked customer asking for 1 rupee is BLOCKED, not AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE.
A customer with no loans has `sum(amount) = NULL`, and `NULL + amount > limit` is NULL, which IF treats as false. Use `COALESCE(sum(amount), 0)`. Case 9 tests exactly this.

exercises.title: Latency percentiles from raw samples
exercises.summary: Nearest-rank p50/p90/p99 with integer rank maths, in Python.

tests.name: ten samples with a long tail

hints: Nearest rank: rank = ceil(p * n / 100), counting from 1. In integers, `-(-p * n // 100)` is the ceiling without any floating-point surprises.
Look at the first test: the mean is 125.1 ms but p50 is 14 ms. One slow request in ten ruins the average, which is why latency is reported as percentiles.

expected: first error: 2026-11-16T10:00:02Z loan-svc timeout calling cbs

exercises.title: An O(1) LRU cache
exercises.summary: std::list + unordered_map of iterators, splice to move to front, evict from the back.
hints: The list holds (key, value) from most recent (front) to least recent (back). The map stores, for each key, an iterator to its list node.
`list_.splice(list_.begin(), list_, it)` moves one node to the front in O(1) without copying, and every iterator stays valid.
Updating an existing key never evicts. Only a NEW key into a full cache evicts `list_.back()`; erase it from the map before you pop it.
